title: University of Manchester develops new methods for treating radioactive waste
summary: New methods for treating radioactive effluents, remediating contaminated groundwater, and stabilizing waste for long-term disposal have been reported by University of Manchester researchers working at the National Nuclear User Facility Radioactive Waste Management and Environmental Remediation (RADER) laboratories in Manchester, England. The research focuses on converting liquid nuclear waste containing the long-lived radioisotope technetium-99 into stable solid waste forms, as well as locking the radioisotope into phosphate minerals and immobilizing it in contaminated groundwater systems.

title: NN Asks: What skill matters most for tomorrow’s nuclear workforce?
summary: Bonnie Scott When someone hears “nuclear,” they think of advanced sciences, specialized technology, or complicated engineering jobs. And while these skills are important, the most critical skill for tomorrow’s nuclear workforce is something we all should recognize in everyday life: a mindset of safety-driven actions and decisions. The basis of our industry is the safe production of reliable electricity. This means ensuring that decisions take the safety of employees and the public into consideration. Yes, the systems used in the nuclear industry are complex and technology continues to evolve rapidly, but the guiding principle for all nuclear work is simple: attention to detail, clear thinking, and smart decision-making where employee and public safety are considered. This mindset must be consistent and deliberate; it is what makes the nuclear industry unique.

title: OPG Begins ‘Comprehensive Assessment’ As Canada SMR Project Faces Delays And Budget Overruns
summary: The first of four BWRX-300 small modular reactors (SMRs) under construction at the Darlington nuclear site in Canada will not be on schedule or to budget, Ontario Power Generation (OPG) has said. OPG said in its 2026 third quarter financial results that it had previously noted that the Darlington New Nuclear Project (DNNP) is subject to “inherent risks and uncertainties that could affect project cost and schedule”.

title: Pouring Of First Concrete Begins For Nuclear Island At China’s Sanao-4
summary: First concrete pouring has begun for the nuclear island of Unit 4 at the Sanao nuclear power station in eastern Chinese province of Zhejiang, project owner China General Nuclear (CGN) announced on Tuesday (10 November). The company said the pouring of first concrete began at 08:28 local time on 10 November, marking the official start of main construction. It said the total volume of concrete poured as of 10 November was approximately 8,820 cubic metres and the process is expected to last 60 hours.

title: UK Nuclear Professionals Confident, But Warn Of Uncertainties And Challenges
summary: Nuclear professionals are confident about the future of the UK industry, but warn that funding uncertainty, skills shortages and challenges delivering major projects could hamper its growth, according to new research from the Nuclear Institute. A survey of Nuclear Institute members found that almost four in five (79.7%) respondents are optimistic about the industry’s future, with a third of these (33.3%) describing themselves as very optimistic. However, the research also highlighted concerns over the industry’s ability to turn ambition into action, with respondents identifying project costs, workforce capacity, regulatory barriers and long-term government support among its most pressing challenges.
